cells.tense: The careful sorting is running now, and the pen is moving in your hand.
cells.act: deepen the mastery by persisting at it
cells.ask: Stay on the piece you're refining well past the point it satisfies you, then take that pass to somebody you feel with and hear their read before you change anything.
cells.core:
You can hear the false note in a thing you're making, the detail most people walk across without noticing, and you stay with it until it sits true. That ear got made by remaining after the work already looked finished to whoever was nearby.

Persistence lasts longer when somebody sees the round before it is sealed. Their read is not applause and not a verdict; it is an angle you cannot stand at from inside your own head. Take the next pass to a person you feel with, let what they say sit, then choose what to keep. The piece stays yours either way.
cells.sheetLine: The thing gets true because you stay in past finished.
cells.verb: Honing — refining what matters from what doesn't through careful private distinction
cells.place: In the middle of a close exchange with someone who matters, where feeling and judgment meet

cells.tense: The sharpening has run past the exchange, cutting at a moment that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.act: make the sacrifice visible without explaining it
cells.ask: Do the next unglamorous piece where somebody you feel with can watch you do it, and say nothing about what the doing costs.
cells.core:
The private sorting has turned into armor. What comes back from another gets weighed before it is allowed near you, and you have been living one beat in front of the exchange — braced, ready, alone with the decision that the tender part is safer held back.

You pay out in the dark: the hours given, the small thing done unseen, and nobody knows to feel it with you. Let somebody you feel with watch the next piece happen, work where it lands. Their seeing does what the hidden version cannot, and the careful eye goes back to what it is for, something you do beside people rather than in front of a panel only you attend.

cells.tense: The checking stopped at a door you're still standing at, and the pen is down.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Offer a thought you hold about a shared thing, then take the answer that comes back as theirs to keep, standing where it stands.
cells.core:
There was a stretch where your read of things got picked over or gently set aside, and the answer you found was to stop offering it at all. The judging still runs, quietly, and almost none of it comes out where somebody could meet it and disagree.

That isn't care now; the door has stayed shut. Say what you actually think about something the two of you share, and let the person you feel with agree or push back as they will. The eye sharpens against something with its own view. Kept behind glass it just gets polished, pointed at nothing that can answer.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped letting anyone tell you which way to look.

cells.tense: The aliveness is already with the two of you, and someone else is holding the pen.
cells.act: savour the realised thing without reaching past it
cells.ask: Point to a small thing you keep going between the two of you, say it is worth keeping, and let that be the last word today.
cells.core:
What you've built with one person, the day-to-day unfancy kind, you describe as nothing special, the sort of thing any two people might manage if they tried. That's your account of it. The tiny repairs behind how it runs, you carry as if they passed through you, not as work you chose and did.

The skill under it belongs to you, and that is not a small claim. Say out loud, to the person you keep it with, that this is worth keeping, then stop. Nothing left to open or fix. What holds between you was made by hand across a long stretch, not handed over. Naming the making is not bragging, only telling the truth about who did it.
